distractorExplanations.b: Maximum LTV is an eligibility guideline; the conforming limit is a dollar cap on loan size set annually by FHFA.
distractorExplanations.c: Ginnie Mae guarantees securities backed by government loans and sets no such minimum; conforming limits are maximums.

prompt: FHA loans are distinctive because they typically require:

options.text: Upfront and annual mortgage insurance premiums with lower down payment options for eligible borrowers
Private mortgage insurance that cancels at 78% LTV, with a 5% minimum down payment
A one-time funding fee instead of monthly insurance, with no down payment for eligible borrowers
Income below 115% of area median and a property located in an eligible rural area

explanation: FHA insurance protects the lender; MIP costs appear in disclosures and affect payment.

distractorExplanations.b: Cancelable PMI and 5% minimums describe conventional loans; FHA uses upfront and annual MIP with a 3.5% minimum down.
distractorExplanations.c: A funding fee with no down payment describes VA loans; FHA charges upfront plus annual mortgage insurance premiums.
distractorExplanations.d: Income caps and rural location are USDA eligibility tests; FHA has no income limit or geographic restriction.

prompt: The VA funding fee on a VA loan generally:

options.text: Is a monthly premium that cancels when the loan reaches 78 percent LTV
Helps sustain the VA loan program and may be financed into the loan amount
Must be paid in cash at closing and cannot be added to the loan amount
Is the same flat amount for every veteran, including those receiving VA disability pay

explanation: Certain veterans are exempt from the funding fee; amount varies by service and use.

distractorExplanations.a: VA loans have no monthly mortgage insurance; the funding fee is a one-time charge, and 78% cancellation is a conventional PMI rule.
distractorExplanations.c: The VA funding fee can be financed into the loan; requiring it in cash confuses it with other closing costs.
distractorExplanations.d: The fee varies by down payment, service type, and first vs subsequent use; veterans receiving VA disability compensation are exempt.

prompt: Compared with a 30-year fixed mortgage, a 15-year fixed generally has:

options.text: Lower monthly payments and less total interest because the rate is lower
The same monthly payment but a lower interest rate, so the loan builds equity much faster
Higher monthly payments but less total interest paid over the life of the loan
Higher monthly payments and more total interest because of the higher rate

explanation: Shorter terms build equity faster and reduce interest cost if the payment is affordable.

distractorExplanations.a: A lower rate helps, but the shorter term raises the monthly payment; payments are higher, not lower, on a 15-year loan.
distractorExplanations.b: Compressing repayment into 15 years raises the payment even at a lower rate; the payment is not the same.
distractorExplanations.d: 15-year rates are typically lower, and fewer years of interest mean less total interest, not more.

prompt: A Home Equity Conversion Mortgage (HECM) reverse mortgage generally requires:

options.text: Borrowers at least age 55 who occupy the home as a principal residence
Borrowers at least age 62 who may rent the home out as an investment property
Borrowers of any age who own the home free and clear and live there full time
Borrowers at least age 62 who occupy the home as a principal residence

explanation: HECMs are FHA-insured reverse mortgages with specific counseling and non-recourse features; borrowers must also complete HUD-approved counseling and meet financial assessment tests.

distractorExplanations.a: Age 55 is used by some proprietary reverse mortgages; the FHA-insured HECM requires borrowers to be at least 62.
distractorExplanations.b: HECMs require the home to be the borrower's principal residence; investment properties are ineligible.
distractorExplanations.c: HECMs require borrowers to be at least 62, and an existing mortgage may be paid off with proceeds rather than owned free and clear.

prompt: A 5/1 adjustable-rate mortgage (ARM) generally means:

options.text: A fixed rate for five years, then annual adjustments based on an index plus margin
A fixed rate for one year, then adjustments every five years based on an index
A fixed rate for five years, then a balloon payment of the remaining balance
A fixed rate for five years, then rate adjustments every six months based on an index plus margin

explanation: ARM disclosures must show initial fixed period, caps, index, margin, and worst-case scenarios.

distractorExplanations.b: The first number is the initial fixed period (five years) and the second is the adjustment frequency (one year).
distractorExplanations.c: A five-year balloon requires a lump-sum payoff; a 5/1 ARM continues amortizing with annual rate adjustments.
distractorExplanations.d: Six-month adjustments after five years describe a 5/6 ARM (common with SOFR); a 5/1 adjusts annually.

prompt: An FHA 203(k) rehabilitation loan is designed to:

options.text: Finance the purchase of a vacant lot and the construction of a new single-family home
Finance purchase or refinance plus eligible repair/improvement costs in one loan
Finance repairs alone, as an unsecured personal loan insured under FHA Title I
Finance a home that already meets FHA standards, with repairs paid by the seller

explanation: 203(k) includes standard and limited versions with consultant/draw requirements for larger projects.

distractorExplanations.a: Lot purchase plus new construction is a construction-to-permanent loan; 203(k) rehabilitates an existing dwelling.
distractorExplanations.c: FHA Title I property improvement loans are separate; 203(k) combines purchase/refinance with repair costs in one mortgage.
distractorExplanations.d: Seller-paid repairs before closing are a standard FHA purchase; 203(k) rolls the borrower's repair costs into the loan.

prompt: A portfolio loan held by the lender on its own books generally:

options.text: Is sold to Fannie Mae with servicing retained by the originating lender
Is securitized through Ginnie Mae as an FHA or VA government loan
Uses the lender's internal guidelines rather than solely selling to GSEs
Is exempt from ATR rules because the lender keeps the credit risk

explanation: Portfolio products can serve non-conforming borrowers but still follow TRID and fair lending rules.

distractorExplanations.a: Selling to Fannie Mae with servicing retained is still a GSE sale; a portfolio loan is held on the lender's own books.
distractorExplanations.b: Ginnie Mae securitization covers government loans sold into MBS; portfolio loans are retained by the lender.
distractorExplanations.d: ATR applies to portfolio loans too; small-creditor portfolio QM offers a compliance path, not an exemption from repayment analysis.

prompt: An 80-10-10 piggyback structure generally involves:

options.text: A first mortgage at 80% LTV, PMI at 10% coverage, and a 10% down payment
A first mortgage at 80% LTV, a 10% gift, and a 10% down payment from savings
A first mortgage at 90% LTV and a 10% down payment, with PMI until 80% LTV
A first mortgage at 80% LTV, a second lien at 10%, and a 10% down payment

explanation: Piggybacks historically helped avoid PMI; second lien terms and qualification matter.

distractorExplanations.a: The structure avoids PMI by using a 10% second lien; it does not involve 10% mortgage insurance coverage.
distractorExplanations.b: An 80-10-10 includes a 10% second mortgage, not a gift; gift-plus-savings would be a 20% down payment.
distractorExplanations.c: A 90% first lien with PMI is a standard conventional loan; the piggyback splits financing into 80% and 10% liens.

prompt: An FHA or VA streamline refinance generally:

options.text: Reduces documentation when replacing an existing FHA/VA loan with a new FHA/VA loan
Allows cash-out up to 85% of value with reduced income and appraisal documentation
Converts an FHA loan to a conventional loan without a new appraisal or credit check
Reduces documentation when refinancing a conventional loan into a new FHA loan

explanation: Streamlines have program-specific eligibility, NTB, and funding fee/MIP rules; the new loan must meet net tangible benefit tests.

distractorExplanations.b: Streamlines are rate/term refinances with little or no cash back; cash-out refinances require full underwriting and appraisal.
distractorExplanations.c: A streamline must refinance FHA into FHA (or VA into VA via IRRRL); moving to conventional requires full underwriting.
distractorExplanations.d: Conventional-to-FHA refinances require full documentation; streamlines are limited to existing FHA or VA loans.

prompt: Non-warrantable condominium projects often face challenges because:

options.text: Condo units cannot be financed with any loan that carries private mortgage insurance
Investor concentration, litigation, or commercial space may exceed agency limits
TRID requires a separate condo disclosure in place of the Loan Estimate
The borrower's DTI exceeds 50%, making the condo unit ineligible for agency sale

explanation: Project approval or limited review status affects eligibility and pricing.

distractorExplanations.a: Warrantable condos can carry PMI; non-warrantable status comes from project-level issues like litigation or investor concentration.
distractorExplanations.c: TRID has no condo-specific disclosure replacing the LE; project eligibility is set by agency condo guidelines.
distractorExplanations.d: Warrantability is a project-level determination; a borrower's DTI affects the loan, not the condo project's status.

prompt: High-balance conforming loans generally:

options.text: Exceed the higher area limits for high-cost counties but remain eligible for GSE purchase
Fall below the baseline conforming limit but carry a higher LTV than standard loans
Exceed the national baseline conforming limit but remain within higher area limits
Exceed the FHA county limit and are insured by FHA under its high-cost area program

explanation: High-cost areas have elevated limits; pricing and LLPAs may differ from standard conforming.

distractorExplanations.a: Loans above the high-cost area limit are jumbo and not GSE-eligible; high-balance loans stay within the higher area limit.
distractorExplanations.b: Loans under the baseline are standard conforming; high-balance refers to amounts above the baseline in high-cost areas.
distractorExplanations.d: High-balance conforming loans are conventional Fannie/Freddie loans, not FHA-insured; FHA has its own county limits.

prompt: Shared appreciation agreements in some equity-sharing products generally:

options.text: Provide monthly payments to an older homeowner, repaid from sale proceeds when they leave
Provide a lower interest rate in exchange for the lender's right to call the loan early
Provide funds as a second lien that accrues interest monthly at a fixed rate
Provide funds to the homeowner in exchange for a future share of home price appreciation

explanation: Equity sharing has distinct repayment and appreciation-sharing terms requiring clear disclosure.

distractorExplanations.a: Monthly payouts repaid on move-out describe a reverse mortgage (HECM), not a share of future appreciation.
distractorExplanations.b: A call option for a lower rate is a callable loan feature; shared appreciation trades funding for a share of future value.
distractorExplanations.c: A fixed-rate interest-bearing second lien is a home equity loan; equity-sharing repayment is tied to future appreciation.

prompt: An interest-only mortgage generally:

options.text: Charges interest without reducing principal during the IO period
Charges less than the full interest, so the unpaid interest is added to principal
Lets the borrower skip payments during the IO period without accruing interest
Reduces principal gradually from the first payment, like a standard 30-year loan

explanation: IO loans defer principal; after the IO period, amortizing payments typically rise. Payment shock at recast and ATR analysis of the fully amortizing payment are core MLO disclosures.

distractorExplanations.b: Adding unpaid interest to principal is negative amortization; an IO payment covers the full interest so the balance stays level.
distractorExplanations.c: Interest accrues and must be paid monthly during the IO period; only principal reduction is deferred, not interest.
distractorExplanations.d: Gradual principal reduction from the first payment describes a fully amortizing loan, not the IO period.

prompt: Alternative documentation (bank statement) loan programs generally carry higher risk because:

options.text: Income is taken from the borrower's stated figure without any third-party verification
Income is inferred from deposits rather than traditional W-2/ tax return verification
Income is verified with W-2s and tax returns, but assets are not checked at all
Income is calculated from the property's rent, without any personal income review

explanation: Non-QM bank statement loans need robust deposit analysis, expense factors, and ATR documentation, which is why lenders apply strong overlays.

distractorExplanations.a: Bank statement loans still verify income through 12-24 months of statements; stated-income lending violates ATR.
distractorExplanations.c: Bank statement programs serve borrowers who lack traditional W-2/tax return income; asset review is still part of underwriting.
distractorExplanations.d: Using property rent to qualify describes a DSCR investor loan, not a bank-statement program based on deposits.

prompt: RESPA Section 8 generally prohibits:

options.text: Charging more than three points and fees on a Qualified Mortgage
A seller requiring the buyer to use a particular title insurance company
Escrow cushions larger than two months of annual escrow disbursements
Kickbacks and unearned fees tied to settlement service referrals

explanation: Section 8 targets referral fees that inflate settlement costs without legitimate services.

distractorExplanations.a: The 3% points-and-fees cap is a Reg Z QM requirement, not a RESPA Section 8 prohibition on kickbacks.
distractorExplanations.b: Seller-required title insurance companies are prohibited by RESPA Section 9, not Section 8's kickback rule.
distractorExplanations.c: The two-month (one-sixth) escrow cushion limit is in RESPA Section 10, not Section 8's anti-kickback rule.

prompt: The right of rescission under TILA for certain refinance transactions on a primary residence generally gives:

options.text: Three business days from the latest of closing, notice, or disclosures
Three calendar days to cancel after funding, including Sundays and holidays
Three business days to cancel a purchase-money loan on a primary residence
Seven business days to cancel after the Loan Estimate is delivered

explanation: TILA rescission applies to certain refinances and home-equity loans secured by the borrower's principal dwelling. The borrower may cancel until midnight of the third business day after the latest of consummation, delivery of the rescission notice, or delivery of the material disclosures.

distractorExplanations.b: Rescission runs three business days (Saturdays count, Sundays and federal holidays do not) from consummation, notice, or disclosures, whichever is last.
distractorExplanations.c: Purchase-money (residential mortgage transaction) loans are exempt from rescission; it applies to certain refinances and home equity loans.
distractorExplanations.d: Seven business days is the LE waiting period before consummation, not the post-closing rescission window.

prompt: Under ECOA (Reg B), when credit is denied, the creditor generally must provide:

options.text: A copy of the credit report used, with the bureau's contact details only
An adverse action notice with specific reasons or instructions to obtain reasons
A written notice within 60 days of the decision stating that the application was denied
A general statement that the applicant did not meet internal standards

explanation: Adverse action notices promote fair lending transparency and applicant rights.

distractorExplanations.a: FCRA requires bureau contact and score disclosure, but ECOA requires an adverse action notice with specific reasons.
distractorExplanations.c: Reg B requires notice within 30 days of a completed application, and it must give or offer the specific reasons.
distractorExplanations.d: Reg B says vague statements like 'failed internal standards' are insufficient; specific principal reasons are required.

prompt: Under FCRA, pulling a consumer credit report for a mortgage application requires:

options.text: A permissible purpose, plus FCRA notice to the consumer after funding
Written authorization from the consumer, renewed every 90 days
A permissible purpose and often written authorization from the consumer
A HMDA disclosure and adverse action notice before the pull

explanation: Permissible purpose and consent protect consumer credit privacy.

distractorExplanations.a: The permissible purpose must exist before the pull; FCRA does not make a post-funding notice the authorization.
distractorExplanations.b: FCRA has no 90-day renewal rule; the consumer's credit application itself creates the permissible purpose.
distractorExplanations.d: HMDA disclosures and adverse action notices are unrelated to accessing credit reports; FCRA requires a permissible purpose.

prompt: ECOA generally prohibits discrimination in credit based on:

options.text: Race, color, religion, national origin, sex, handicap, and familial status as listed under fair lending law
Race, color, religion, sex, marital status, age, and the applicant's length of employment or job type
Race, color, religion, national origin, sex, and age, but not marital status or receipt of public assistance
Race, color, religion, national origin, sex, marital status, age (with exceptions), receipt of public assistance

explanation: Protected classes under ECOA and FHA guide fair lending compliance. ECOA also protects good-faith exercise of rights under consumer credit laws.

distractorExplanations.a: Handicap and familial status are Fair Housing Act bases; ECOA covers marital status, age, and public assistance instead.
distractorExplanations.b: Length of employment is a legitimate underwriting factor, not an ECOA prohibited basis.
distractorExplanations.c: Reg B expressly protects marital status and income from public assistance programs; creditors may not exclude them as prohibited bases.

prompt: TRID changed circumstances that allow revised Loan Estimates generally include:

options.text: Events like interest rate locks after LE issuance or appraisal-driven value changes
Fee increases the lender documents internally, even when no new information has come to light
Borrower complaints about fees, which reset all tolerances once a new LE is sent
Any event discovered after the Closing Disclosure is issued, up to 60 days later

explanation: Changed circumstance rules limit tolerance violations and require timely redisclosure.

distractorExplanations.b: A changed circumstance needs an extraordinary event, new information, or inaccurate information relied on, not internal paperwork.
distractorExplanations.c: Complaints are not changed circumstances; a revised LE resets baselines only when a valid trigger exists and is sent within 3 business days.
distractorExplanations.d: Changed circumstances justify a revised LE before the CD; the 60-day window applies to post-consummation tolerance refunds.

prompt: HOEPA (high-cost mortgage) coverage generally triggers when:

options.text: The borrower requests a 30-year fixed rate
Points and fees or APR exceed specific regulatory thresholds for a home loan
The property has more than one bedroom
The loan is sold to any GSE investor

explanation: HOEPA adds extra disclosures and restrictions for high-cost home loans.

distractorExplanations.a: Fixed rate alone does not trigger HOEPA.
distractorExplanations.c: Bedroom count is irrelevant.
distractorExplanations.d: GSE sale alone does not define HOEPA status.

prompt: HPML appraisal rules generally require:

options.text: An automated valuation model, with the result given to the borrower at closing
A verbal value estimate from the appraiser before the lender orders the report
A written appraisal and delivery to the borrower before closing
A desktop appraisal without interior inspection, shared on borrower request

explanation: Borrowers receive copies and may obtain additional appraisal under certain conditions; this applies to many higher-priced first-lien mortgages.

distractorExplanations.a: HPML rules require a written appraisal with an interior inspection by a certified or licensed appraiser, not an AVM.
distractorExplanations.b: HPML appraisals must be written, and copies delivered at least three business days before consummation.
distractorExplanations.d: HPML rules require a physical interior inspection, and the copy must be provided free without waiting for a request.

prompt: HMDA Loan Application Register (LAR) reporting generally helps regulators:

options.text: Verify each borrower's identity and screen loan applicants against OFAC sanctions lists
Set annual conforming loan limits based on reported home prices in each county
Track MLO licensing status and continuing education through annual NMLS filings
Monitor fair lending patterns and market activity by collecting application and loan data

explanation: HMDA data supports public disclosure and regulatory fair lending analysis.

distractorExplanations.a: Identity verification and OFAC screening are BSA/AML and sanctions duties, not HMDA's data-reporting purpose.
distractorExplanations.b: Conforming limits are set by FHFA using its house price index, not from HMDA LAR data.
distractorExplanations.c: Licensing and CE tracking happen in NMLS under the SAFE Act; HMDA collects application and loan data.

prompt: Regulation B appraisal copy rules generally require creditors to:

options.text: Provide applicants copies of appraisals and written valuations
Provide copies of appraisals only if the applicant requests them in writing
Provide copies of appraisals for loans that close, but not for denied applications
Provide copies of appraisals after charging the applicant a separate copy fee

explanation: Applicants may review valuations promptly even if credit is denied; the rule covers appraisals and written valuations developed in connection with the application.

distractorExplanations.b: Since 2014, Reg B requires creditors to provide copies promptly without a request; a written request is no longer needed.
distractorExplanations.c: Copies are due promptly or three business days before consummation, and also when the application is denied or withdrawn.
distractorExplanations.d: Reg B bars charging for the copy itself, although a reasonable fee for the appraisal may be charged.

prompt: Qualified Mortgage (QM) safe harbor vs rebuttable presumption generally differs in:

options.text: Whether the loan's points and fees fall under the 3% cap that applies to every QM
How much legal protection the creditor receives if the borrower later challenges ATR compliance
Whether the creditor must verify the borrower's income and assets before the loan is consummated
Whether the loan may include negative amortization, interest-only, or balloon payment features

explanation: Safe harbor QM offers stronger defense; rebuttable presumption QM allows borrower challenge with evidence.

distractorExplanations.a: The 3% points-and-fees cap applies to both safe harbor and rebuttable QMs; the split depends on APR vs APOR pricing.
distractorExplanations.c: Verification is required for QMs and non-QMs alike; safe harbor vs rebuttable presumption concerns litigation protection.
distractorExplanations.d: No QM of either type may have negative amortization or IO features (balloons only in narrow small-creditor cases); that is not the distinction between them.

prompt: TRID generally requires the consumer to receive the Closing Disclosure:

options.text: At least one business day before consummation, as with the old HUD-1
At the closing table, together with the note and the security instrument
At least three business days before consummation
At least seven business days before consummation, the same as the LE

explanation: Three-day CD rule helps borrowers compare final terms to the Loan Estimate; limited redisclosure rules apply if certain changes occur.

distractorExplanations.a: The one-day pre-closing review was a HUD-1 rule under old RESPA; the CD must be received three business days before.
distractorExplanations.b: Receipt at the closing table is too late; TRID requires CD receipt at least three business days before consummation.
distractorExplanations.d: Seven business days is the waiting period after LE delivery; the CD rule is three business days before consummation.

prompt: FCRA dispute procedures generally allow consumers to:

options.text: Remove accurate negative items older than two years by filing a written dispute
Block lenders from pulling their credit while a dispute is pending with a bureau
Have the lender correct the credit report directly during underwriting
Challenge inaccurate credit report information with bureaus and data furnishers

explanation: Bureaus must investigate disputes and correct or delete inaccurate/unverifiable data.

distractorExplanations.a: Accurate negative information can be reported for seven years (bankruptcies up to ten); disputes address inaccuracy.
distractorExplanations.b: A pending dispute does not bar permissible-purpose pulls; it obligates the bureau to investigate, usually within 30 days.
distractorExplanations.c: Lenders cannot alter bureau files; corrections come from bureau and furnisher investigations or a rapid rescore based on them.

prompt: The ATR rule's eight underwriting factors generally include:

options.text: Income/assets, employment, monthly payment, simultaneous mortgage obligations, other debt, DTI/residual, and credit history
Income/assets, employment, credit history, the property's appraised value, expected appreciation, and the LTV ratio
Income/assets, employment, monthly payment, and DTI, with credit history excluded under ECOA to prevent discrimination
Income/assets, employment, other debt, DTI, and credit history, with the monthly payment measured at the introductory teaser rate

explanation: Creditors must consider comprehensive repayment ability under Reg Z ATR.

distractorExplanations.b: Appreciation forecasts and LTV are collateral considerations; ATR's eight factors focus on the borrower's capacity to repay.
distractorExplanations.c: Credit history is one of the eight ATR factors; ECOA does not bar considering it as a legitimate underwriting factor.
distractorExplanations.d: ATR requires the payment at the fully indexed rate (or the maximum in the first five years), not the introductory teaser rate.

prompt: Higher-priced mortgage loans (HPMLs) secured by a first lien on a principal dwelling generally require:

options.text: A second appraisal on every HPML refinance, ordered by the lender at the borrower's expense
An escrow account for property taxes and insurance for a minimum period after consummation
Private mortgage insurance for at least five years after consummation, even below 80% LTV
An escrow account for taxes and insurance that the borrower may cancel after 12 months

explanation: HPML rules add escrow (and appraisal) protections on many first-lien principal-dwelling loans; ATR and TILA still apply.

distractorExplanations.a: A second appraisal applies to certain HPML flips, not every refinance, and the borrower cannot be charged for it.
distractorExplanations.c: HPML rules require escrow for at least five years; they do not mandate private mortgage insurance.
distractorExplanations.d: HPML escrows generally must be kept at least five years, and cancellation requires LTV under 80% and no delinquency.

prompt: SAFE Act continuing education for MLOs generally requires:

options.text: Annual completion of 8 hours of CE, with no federal law or ethics content required
Completion of 20 hours of CE every two years, focused on nontraditional lending
Retaking the national test every three years instead of completing annual CE
Annual completion of federal and state CE including ethics and federal law components

explanation: States set hour requirements within SAFE minimums; failure can suspend licensure.

distractorExplanations.a: The 8 annual hours must include 3 hours of federal law, 2 of ethics, and 2 on nontraditional lending.
distractorExplanations.b: Twenty hours is the pre-licensing education minimum; SAFE CE is at least 8 hours every year, not biennial.
distractorExplanations.c: The national test must be retaken only after a licensing lapse of five years or more; CE is the annual requirement.

prompt: An MLO's NMLS unique identifier generally must be:

options.text: Disclosed on loan documents and marketing as required by state and federal rules
Disclosed on the loan application, but omitted from advertising to avoid confusion
Disclosed to the borrower verbally at application, with no written disclosure needed
Shared with the processor so loans can be submitted under the MLO's identifier

explanation: NMLS ID promotes accountability and consumer lookup of originator credentials.

distractorExplanations.b: Reg Z and state rules require the NMLS ID on key loan documents, and states generally require it in advertising too.
distractorExplanations.c: Reg Z requires the NMLS ID in writing on the application, note, and security instrument, not just verbally.
distractorExplanations.d: The NMLS ID belongs to the individual MLO; letting others originate under it is unlicensed activity.

prompt: Honest advertising of mortgage rates and terms generally requires:

options.text: Showing the lowest rate available to top-tier borrowers, with the APR placed in a footnote
Representing terms actually available to typical qualified applicants with required disclosures
Listing the monthly payment and rate, with trigger-term disclosures offered upon request
Advertising a fixed rate that later converts to an adjustable rate, with the change disclosed only after application

explanation: Truth in advertising and UDAAP principles prohibit bait-and-switch promotions.

distractorExplanations.a: Reg Z requires the APR with equal prominence when a rate is stated, and rates must be reasonably available, not top-tier.
distractorExplanations.c: Payment amounts are trigger terms, so required disclosures must appear in the ad itself, not on request.
distractorExplanations.d: Ads must clearly disclose rate changes; hiding an ARM conversion until after application is misleading.

prompt: Steering a borrower to a higher-cost loan primarily because it pays the MLO more generally violates:

options.text: RESPA Section 8 rules prohibiting referral fees between the MLO and the borrower
HMDA rules requiring the MLO to report the higher-cost loan to regulators as a steering violation
Fair lending and LO compensation rules prohibiting predatory steering for personal gain
SAFE Act rules capping MLO commissions at a fixed percentage of the loan amount

explanation: Steering for compensation harms borrowers and triggers RESPA/TILA/ECOA scrutiny.

distractorExplanations.a: Section 8 targets kickbacks among settlement providers; steering for higher pay is addressed by LO comp and fair lending rules.
distractorExplanations.b: HMDA collects pricing data for analysis; it does not classify individual loans as steering violations.
distractorExplanations.d: The SAFE Act governs licensing and does not cap commissions; steering is governed by Reg Z anti-steering rules.

prompt: Before consummation, the borrower generally must receive:

options.text: A Good Faith Estimate early and a HUD-1 settlement statement one day before closing
The Closing Disclosure early, with the Loan Estimate delivered at the closing table
The Loan Estimate early, with the Closing Disclosure delivered after funding
TRID disclosures including the Loan Estimate early and Closing Disclosure before closing

explanation: Timely LE/CD delivery is a core consumer protection under TRID.

distractorExplanations.a: The GFE and HUD-1 were replaced by the LE and CD for most closed-end mortgages in October 2015.
distractorExplanations.b: The order is reversed: the LE comes within 3 business days of application and the CD at least 3 business days before closing.
distractorExplanations.c: The CD must be received before consummation, at least three business days ahead, not after funding.

prompt: An affiliated business arrangement referral to a title company generally requires:

options.text: A timely AfBA disclosure of the relationship and estimated charges
An AfBA disclosure, after which the borrower may be required to use the affiliate
A verbal mention of the affiliation at closing, with the charges shown on the CD
A disclosure of the relationship, with referral fees paid to the MLO per closed file

explanation: AfBA disclosures explain the relationship and charges; RESPA still generally bars requiring a particular title company, so disclosure is not a license to require it.

distractorExplanations.b: Disclosure does not authorize mandatory use; RESPA generally bars requiring an affiliated title company as a condition.
distractorExplanations.c: The AfBA disclosure must be written and given at or before the referral, not verbally at closing.
distractorExplanations.d: AfBA compliance allows ownership returns, not per-referral payments; fees for referrals remain Section 8 kickbacks.

prompt: The LO compensation rule generally prohibits:

options.text: Paying originators a fixed percentage of the loan amount on each closed loan
Varying originator compensation based on loan terms or conditions
Paying originators more for higher loan volume or a larger number of closings
Reducing originator compensation to cover an unforeseen closing cost increase

explanation: Comp may not be tied to rate, price, or product to steer for higher pay.

distractorExplanations.a: A fixed percentage of the loan amount is permitted (with small-loan limits); the ban is on comp that varies with loan terms.
distractorExplanations.c: Volume-based compensation is permitted because volume is not a loan term; terms such as rate or fees cannot drive pay.
distractorExplanations.d: Reg Z allows an originator to reduce comp to cover unforeseen increases in third-party settlement costs.

prompt: An MLO who owns an appraisal management relationship must generally:

options.text: Share the contract price and target value so the appraiser can confirm it
Select appraisers based on how often their values support the contract price
Maintain appraiser independence and avoid influencing value conclusions
Review the appraisal and adjust the value if comparable sales seem too low

explanation: Appraiser independence rules under Dodd-Frank and USPAP ethics prohibit undue influence.

distractorExplanations.a: Providing a target value to hit is undue influence; sharing the contract is fine, but no value should be suggested.
distractorExplanations.b: Choosing appraisers for hitting values is a classic independence violation under Reg Z valuation rules.
distractorExplanations.d: Only the appraiser may change a value; originators can request reconsideration of value with data but cannot alter the report.

prompt: When an MLO discovers material misstatements on an application, ethical practice generally requires:

options.text: Submitting the file and letting quality control catch the misstatement after closing
Having the borrower sign a corrected 1003 at closing while underwriting still relies on the original
Telling the borrower about the issue but leaving it up to them whether to correct the file before submission
Correcting the record, notifying compliance/supervision, and not submitting false data to underwriting

explanation: Fraudulent misrepresentation exposes the MLO, company, and borrower to civil and criminal liability.

distractorExplanations.a: Knowingly passing false data to underwriting and relying on post-closing QC makes the MLO complicit in fraud.
distractorExplanations.b: Leaving underwriting with the false original means the decision still rests on misstated data; corrections must come first.
distractorExplanations.c: The MLO cannot submit known false information even if the borrower declines to fix it; escalation and correction are required.

prompt: Redlining as a fair lending violation generally means:

options.text: Denying or limiting credit in geographic areas based on prohibited characteristics
Charging higher rates to individual borrowers based on their race rather than credit risk
Pricing loans in flood zones higher based on FEMA maps and insurance costs
Steering minority buyers toward certain neighborhoods during the home search

explanation: Redlining is illegal discrimination in lending patterns, not neutral risk-based marketing.

distractorExplanations.b: Individual pricing discrimination is disparate treatment; redlining refers to excluding or limiting credit in whole areas.
distractorExplanations.c: Pricing for documented geographic hazards is a legitimate risk factor, not discrimination based on neighborhood demographics.
distractorExplanations.d: Directing buyers toward or away from neighborhoods is real estate steering under the Fair Housing Act, not lending redlining.

prompt: Predatory lending characteristics may include:

options.text: A rate/term refinance that lowers the rate and pays modest documented fees
Repeated refinances that strip equity (loan flipping) and hidden excessive fees
A cash-out refinance used to consolidate high-rate debt with disclosed costs
Offering an ARM with clear disclosure of caps, index, margin, and worst case

explanation: Flipping and fee packing harm vulnerable borrowers and trigger UDAAP/enforcement action.

distractorExplanations.a: A transparent rate reduction with documented fees provides a net tangible benefit; that is ordinary, not predatory, lending.
distractorExplanations.c: Debt consolidation with disclosed costs can be legitimate; predatory lending involves flipping, fee packing, or concealment.
distractorExplanations.d: Fully disclosed ARMs are legitimate products; predatory lending involves equity stripping and hidden or excessive fees.

prompt: GLBA privacy notices for mortgage customers generally require:

options.text: A notice only when NPI is shared with affiliates, with no notice owed to new customers at account opening
Written opt-in consumer consent before any NPI is shared with nonaffiliated third parties for marketing
Initial and annual notice of information sharing practices and opt-out rights where applicable
Annual privacy notices that customers must sign and return before closing

explanation: GLBA governs nonpublic personal information handling and affiliate sharing rules.

distractorExplanations.a: GLBA requires an initial notice at the start of the customer relationship; affiliate sharing is covered separately by FCRA.
distractorExplanations.b: GLBA uses an opt-out model for most nonaffiliated sharing, not opt-in consent (some states impose stricter rules).
distractorExplanations.d: Privacy notices are delivered, not signed and returned; annual notices can be skipped if policies are unchanged and sharing is limited.

prompt: SAFE Act registration generally means MLOs must:

options.text: Hold a single national NMLS license that replaces separate state licensing
Register through NMLS once, with background checks and credit reports required only at initial application
Obtain federal registration whether employed by a bank or by a nonbank mortgage company
Maintain active state license/federal registration through NMLS with background checks and CE

explanation: Dual state and federal registration enforces standards through NMLS.

distractorExplanations.a: NMLS is a registry and system of record; licenses are still issued by each state where the MLO originates.
distractorExplanations.b: Licensing requires ongoing renewal, CE, and updated background/credit authorizations, not a one-time check.
distractorExplanations.c: Federal registration applies to depository-institution employees; nonbank MLOs need a state license.

prompt: TRID tolerance buckets (zero, 10%, unlimited) generally classify:

options.text: Which closing cost increases over the Loan Estimate are allowed or must be cured
Which fees count toward the 3% points-and-fees cap that applies to Qualified Mortgages
Which APR changes require a corrected CD and a new three-business-day waiting period
Which settlement providers the borrower may shop for after receiving the LE

explanation: TRID tolerances limit how much charges may rise from the Loan Estimate. Zero tolerance covers fees paid to the creditor, mortgage broker, or an affiliate of either, transfer taxes, and services the borrower cannot shop for; 10% aggregate covers recording fees and shoppable services chosen from the creditor's list. Excess must be refunded within 60 days of consummation.

distractorExplanations.b: The points-and-fees cap is a QM/ATR test; tolerance buckets limit how much LE fees may rise at closing.
distractorExplanations.c: APR accuracy redisclosure triggers a new three-day wait; tolerance buckets govern increases in specific closing fees.
distractorExplanations.d: Shoppable status influences the bucket, but the buckets themselves classify allowable fee increases and cures.

prompt: UDAAP (Unfair, Deceptive, or Abusive Acts or Practices) enforcement in mortgage generally targets:

options.text: Conduct that violates a state licensing rule, such as a late NMLS renewal filing
Conduct that misleads borrowers or takes unreasonable advantage of lack of understanding
Any lending practice that results in a borrower default or foreclosure later on
Charging fees that exceed the 10% tolerance bucket at closing on the CD

explanation: CFPB UDAAP authority addresses hidden traps and abusive sales tactics.

distractorExplanations.a: Late renewals are licensing matters handled by state regulators; UDAAP targets misleading or exploitative conduct toward consumers.
distractorExplanations.c: Default alone does not prove UDAAP; the standard looks at deceptive, unfair, or abusive conduct, not loan outcomes.
distractorExplanations.d: Tolerance violations are TRID disclosure issues cured with refunds; UDAAP covers deceptive, unfair, or abusive conduct.
